translationRepairs: During palace games Wu Di pointed out the boy to the witless Hui: 'That one is your heir.'

Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'

Before invents "witless" and mistranslates 兒 as "heir," but the proposal wrongly makes Emperor Wu take the princes' hands; after 惠帝來朝 the hand-taking continues Hui's greeting, and 惠帝乃止 confirms he stopped that greeting when Wu said 是汝兒也.
Pan Yue forged spirit-prayer lines; drunk Yu copied them under Chen Wu's orders.

She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

Before wrongly credits Chen Wu with ordering the copy; Chinese has Pan Yue draft the prayer-like text and 小婢承福 deliver paper, brush, and draft so the drunken Crown Prince writes it. The revision preserves his established title and renders 小婢 naturally.
An imperial train stripped Yu at Eastern Palace.

Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Tong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Eastern Martial Duke; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Tutor He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the Crown Prince as a commoner.

Before collapses the deposition embassy into a nameless "imperial train"; Chinese names 尚書和郁, 解結, 梁王肜, 淮南王允, 東武公澹, 趙王倫, and 太保何劭. The revision restores every envoy using their established full names and titles and makes the long list legible in English.

Before replaces the rhyme with truncated commentary and a stray quote mark; Chinese quotes the full children's verse 南風起兮吹白沙…, which the proposed rendering restores.

沙門 is the childhood byname Shamen; "White Sand" confuses it with 白沙 in the preceding rhyme, and the proposed "Shamen" restores the gloss.

Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
This sentence is still Yu's first-person letter; before shifts to third person and paraphrases away the title 宜城君, while the proposed wording keeps 自宜城君亡 and 不見存恤 in first person.

When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
In the patent formula 衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈, 伊 is the envoy's name and 策 the announcement verb; treating "Yi Ce" as a personal name is wrong, and the proposed wording restores that parse.
